stories.key_takeaway: Tencent's reported $7 billion, five-year lease of about 100,000 advanced AI chips in Oracle's Southeast Asian data centers is the largest test yet of the remote-access gap in U.S. export controls, which Congress is trying to close.

pull_quote.text: Our export controls are only as strong as the weakest link, and right now, the CCP has a real tool to sidestep these prohibitions.

stories.headline: Volantis Raises $88 Million to Break AI's Memory Wall With Laser Links

pull_quote.text: No one is going to win a Nobel Prize if our project works, but the good news is, they won't need to.

stories.headline: JERA, Dell and RHAELM Plan $15 Billion, 400MW AI Data Center Inside a Japanese Power Plant
stories.key_takeaway: By putting a 400MW AI campus behind the meter at its Chiba power station, JERA, Dell and RHAELM aim to skip Japan's grid queues and build a model they can repeat to reach multi-gigawatt AI capacity in the 2030s.

pull_quote.text: Deploying AI infrastructure at national scale requires a foundation built for control, flexibility and growth from day one.
pull_quote.role: President, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Dell Technologies

stories.article_excerpt: Japan's biggest power company has decided the fastest way to get electricity to an AI data center is to stop sending it anywhere else.

pull_quote.text: Prefer Astra when peak score matters; prefer 6.1 Sol when cost and throughput matter.

stories.headline: UCLA's Light-Based AI Screens 15 Videos at Once for Deepfakes With Nearly 98% Accuracy
stories.key_takeaway: Aydogan Ozcan's UCLA lab built a hybrid detector that does part of its work with light passing through optics, screening 15 videos in one pass with 97.79% accuracy and 99.86% sensitivity, as a low-energy, hard-to-fool first filter in front of heavier digital models.

pull_quote.text: Integrating optical computation into AI inference enables simultaneous gains in throughput, energy efficiency, and adversarial robustness—three properties that are difficult to achieve together in purely digital systems.
pull_quote.attribution: Parnian Ghapandar Kashani, Shiqi Chen and Aydogan Ozcan

stories.headline: AI Agents Can Radicalize Each Other, New Study Warns
stories.key_takeaway: A two-agent simulation found that an influencer LLM can push a persona-playing LLM toward more extreme beliefs, including more willingness to endorse violent protest and war, and that reinforcing beliefs the agent already holds works better than arguing for new ones.

pull_quote.text: Both mechanisms radicalize the target, with resonance producing consistently stronger effects than persuasion.
pull_quote.attribution: Ozgur Can Seckin, Filippo Menczer et al.
pull_quote.role: Authors, AI Agents are Vulnerable to Radicalization (arXiv:2609.38296)

pull_quote.text: Nobody wants to be fired by a machine.
